definition: Enamor means to fill with love or fascination.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word enamor. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know enamor should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: One week at her grandmother's forge was enough to enamor Lena of blacksmithing for life.
Please is the faintest glow — a pleased visitor nods and moves on; it stops far short of enamor.
Charm goes further than please but stops short of enamor: a charmed guest smiles all evening; an enamored one is still talking about it in June.

Bewitch means to fascinate so completely that it feels like a spell — stronger and stranger than enamor. Being enamored is warm, human affection that keeps drawing you back; being bewitched hints that your judgment has been taken over by something you cannot resist.

Captivate means to seize delighted attention and hold it — a captivating speaker owns the room for as long as she talks. Enamor goes deeper and lasts longer: it plants real affection, so the pull is still there long after the performance has ended.

to break the spell and let the fondness drain out
An amateur astronomer in Ohio spotted the comet two nights before the big observatories did.
Enamor means to fill with love or fascination.
The planetarium's creaky star projector enamored generations of schoolchildren; ushers joked that half the city's astronomers could date their careers to one field trip under its painted dome.
Enamor means to fill with love or lasting fascination, and it usually appears in the passive: you are enamored of — or with — something.
It is stronger than 'like' and warmer than 'impress': what enamors you pulls you back again and again.
Enamor is a touch bookish and almost always passive: enamored of a city, enamored with a craft.
For quick attraction, charmed or taken with is lighter.
Its unit-mate enthrall grips the attention; enamor claims the heart — an enthralled visitor cannot look away, while an enamored one comes back the next day in love.
And nobody is enamored of a tax form; keep it for real affection.

Maya transferred to Kettering High in October, certain she would hate everything about it.
Then a scheduling error placed her in the basement studio of KTRH, the student-run radio station, as a fourth-period aide.

The station did not just amuse her; it began to enamor her of the whole craft of broadcasting -- the switchboard's lights, the hush before the mic went live, the way a good segue could make two songs shake hands.
By December she was staying long after the bell, rebuilding playlists nobody had asked her to touch.
Years later she would tell interns that the schedule mix-up was the luckiest thing that ever happened to her.
